before.title: Tight turn off the boards
before.objective: Pair a visible edge-work cue (a tight inside turn away from a forechecker) with the same geometry-comparison read used throughout the bank, at an age band where no skating cue currently exists.
before.briefing: YOU carries the puck along the near boards in the neutral zone and has just executed a tight inside turn to escape F1's forecheck. Gold1 supports through the middle of the ice; Gold2 is farther along, still tight to the boards. Attacking direction is up-ice toward the +x end (not rendered as a net in this neutral-zone freeze).
cues: YOU has just turned away from F1, toward the middle of the ice.
F1 was already committed wide, toward the boards, before the turn.
Gold1 is open through the middle; Gold2 is in the same near-boards band as F1.
before.limits: Static original practice illustration; movement and outcomes are not simulated. The turn itself is described in the briefing/cues, not rendered as two states -- the engine (per experimentalBankCore.js) gives every actor exactly one static facing angle, never a two-pose sequence. Position references are illustrative, not graded target zones.
before.prompt: YOU just used a tight inside edge to turn away from F1 along the boards. Which teammate does that turn open up?

options.text: Gold 1, now open through the middle
Gold 2, still in the same near-boards band as F1
Neither -- F1's position already threatens both lanes equally

before.explanation: At this exact freeze F1 is geometrically about 6.0m off BOTH the YOU-Gold1 and YOU-Gold2 lines (identical perpendicular distance) -- F1 does not yet block either lane outright. The real distinction is lateral band: F1 sits at y=-11.5, within half a metre of Gold2's y=-10.5, but Gold1 sits at y=-3, roughly 8.5m of lateral ice away from F1. F1 can recover into Gold2's band far faster than into Gold1's, which is why Gold1 is the safer read even though neither lane is literally cut off yet.

before.briefing: YOU has the puck; Gold1 is the current best passing option, well off F1's lane (F1 is currently below and to YOU's side, not between YOU and Gold1). This question adds a stated hypothetical: F1 closes hard and gets across the passing lane. The RENDERED scene does not change -- per the schema (one static 'setup' per scenario, shared by every question on it), F1's actual drawn position must stay identical to draft26-u11-cause-001-q1's; the hypothetical exists only in the prompt text, exactly like the bank's real 'Imagine...'/'Suppose...' questions.

before.prompt: Suppose F1 reads the pass, closes hard, and gets between YOU and Gold1, cutting off that lane entirely. What should YOU do differently?
before.explanation: This is the family's defining move: state one explicit hypothetical change to a single actor, and require the learner to update their read rather than repeat the baseline answer. Expected directions: hold the puck, look for a second option, or delay -- there is no objective answer key for 'explain' questions in the real engine (see schemaValidation below); this explanation text is shown to every player regardless of what they typed, as coaching context, not a graded comparison.
